$meta.comment: Canonical Figma <-> code mapping (ADR-0010). Human-readable view: Architecture.md §3.1. Every entry's code file must carry `// figma: node-id=<nodeId>` in its header. Components are added here in the same PR that creates them (Phase 2+); nodeId values are looked up in Figma dev mode or via MCP at build time.
$meta.status: pre-Phase-2: paths reserved, nodeId filled in when each component is built

Atom/Button.notes: CVA variant=filled|outline|white|transparent|destructive (Figma 'Distructive'); Hover/Selected are CSS states. 'Selected' was renamed from 'Active' in Figma 2026-07-20 (ticket #42, mis-naming corrected upstream) — re-fetched node confirms every style's State enum is now Default/Hover/Selected, same fills/text as before the rename, no pixel change. Modelled via `aria-pressed:` (not `active:` — CSS :active means 'being pressed', a different, non-persistent thing), same idiom as Atom/Button-Toggle; caller sets the standard `aria-pressed` attribute, not a new prop. 'With icon'/'With text' modelled as presence of the `icon`/`children` props; icon-only requires aria-label (type-enforced). Figma's Filled/Selected instance has drifted padding (uniform 8px vs 4px/8px elsewhere) — treated as auto-layout drift, not modelled. Hover fill/stroke use the dedicated surface-hover / border-hover semantic tokens (added 2026-07-20; same stone-300/stone-500 primitives, named for their role). Dark mode (ticket #42): surface-raised/surface-hover/surface/border/border-hover/text/text-muted/priority-urgent-bg now carry a dark override in design/tokens.json → emitted as a `[data-theme="dark"]` block in app/theme.css by `pnpm sync:tokens` (that attribute is what @ladle/react's Light/Dark toggle sets on <html>). No Figma dark-mode frames exist for this node, so the dark shades (stone-700/800/900/400, red-950 — all newly added stock-Tailwind primitives, no one-off hex) are this fix's own pick, not a Figma-sourced value; component classes needed zero changes (no `dark:` utilities) since they were already semantic-token-only — the bug was entirely in the token pipeline, which previously emitted no dark values and no dark selector at all. FIXED 2026-07-20 (#43): Fixed for ticket #43 (2026-07-20): root class was `justify-center`, but every sampled Button/Default variant is a hug-sized row with no `justifyContent` override (Figma default packed/left) — invisible on hug-sized standalone buttons, but wrong once a caller stretches the button full-width (Atom/Dropdown's option-list slot does exactly that) Changed to `justify-start`; no visual change to any existing Button story. UPDATED for ticket #52 (2026-07-20): Figma reworked every colour role to carry a per-state Default/Hover/Selected variation instead of Default + one ad-hoc hover — re-fetched node confirms the ticket's own state matrix verbatim, no discrepancy. Filled hover bg stone-200->stone-400 (new `surface-raised-hover` token, was wrongly stone-300/`surface-hover`); Filled selected bg -> stone-300 (new `surface-raised-selected`, was previously unchanged from default). White selected bg -> stone-50 (new `surface-selected`, was previously unchanged). Outline hover border -> stone-700 (new `border-hover-strong`; `border-hover` itself stays stone-500, since Atom/Input-field's Hover stroke did NOT move — the two roles that used to share `border-hover` have diverged, open question recorded in docs/design-tokens.md); Outline selected border -> stone-400 (new `border-selected`, was wrongly reverting to plain `border`). Distructive gained real Hover (red-200, new `priority-urgent-bg-hover`) and Selected (red-100, new `priority-urgent-bg-selected`) backgrounds — previously this style had no state override at all; its text stays `priority-urgent` in every state. `surface-hover` (stone-300) loses its only consumer here but is kept, unconsumed, per the ticket (may still be wanted elsewhere). See docs/design-tokens.md for the full table and the state-token naming convention future components should follow. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20, supersedes #52's matrix): Figma added a FOURTH state (Active) and redistributed the values - what #52 recorded as Hover is now Active (pressed), Hover took a milder new value, and Selected no longer changes fill/stroke at all, only the text (-> text/stone-950). Re-fetched node 3623:4346 confirms: Filled stone-200/stone-300/stone-400, White white/stone-50/stone-100, Outline stroke stone-300/stone-400/stone-700, Distructive red-50/red-100/red-200 (Distructive Selected is identical to Default, text stays red-400 throughout). Transparent has NO fill in any state - so a transparent button has no pointer affordance at all; flagged as a design question in docs/design-tokens.md, not invented here. Modelled as `hover:` + `active:` (CSS :active is exactly Figma's new 'being pressed' state) + `aria-pressed:text-text`; the three compose because Selected touches only `color` while Hover/Active touch only background/border - a stated product requirement (a selected button must still react to the pointer), so no aria-pressed:bg-*/border-* override may ever be added. Tokens renamed to the role/-hover/-active scale; the *-selected colour tokens #52 added were removed (Selected has no background of its own). Stories cut from 10 exports to 2 (StateMatrix + args-driven Playground) so Button no longer fills the Ladle sidebar with one heading per state.

Atom/Tag.notes: Figma 'Color' axis → semantic CVA variant: Grey→neutral, Red→urgent, Yellow→medium, Blue→mid, Green→low (matches card priority enum)

Atom/Input-field.notes: Figma 'Trekking-icon' is a misnomer for the TRAILING icon → code prop `trailingIcon`. 'Field'+'Title' → `label` (requires `id`, type-enforced, since an RSC cannot useId); 'Content' → native placeholder/value; 'Button' SLOT → `button` named slot (not a hardcoded Button instance, per CLAUDE.md). NOT MODELLED: Figma's 'Text' bool can hide the whole input row, leaving only the button slot — meaningless for an input atom, flagged for triage. FIXED 2026-07-20 (#44): every padding/gap was already numerically correct against the dev-ready node; the reported 'wrong spacing' was the container's `items-center`, which centers the shorter 32px leading+text column inside the row's real 40px height (set by the trailing icon), adding a phantom ~4px offset absent from Figma's implicit top alignment - corrected to `items-start`. UPDATED 2026-07-20 (#53): re-fetched node shows the semantic variables were reworked since #44 and the set now has three real, distinct container strokes: Default stone-300 (content stone-300 placeholder), Hover stone-500 (content stone-300 placeholder), Active stone-400 (content stone-950 typed). The invented 2px focus-within ring from #44 (which reused border-hover because no Focus state existed) is removed; focus is now expressed as `focus-within:border-border-selected` (new stone-400/stone-500(dark) token, design/tokens.json), matching the fetched Active stroke exactly — no ring/outline. FLAGGED HONESTLY, not resolved silently: (a) Figma names this third state 'Active', not 'Focus' — mapping it to `:focus-within` is this atom's reading (it's the only interaction state left in the set and its sample shows a typed value), needs design confirmation; (b) a 1px border-colour change is a weak focus affordance for keyboard users and Figma offers nothing stronger in this node — flagged as a design question, no ring/outline was invented to compensate. Deliberately NOT `accent`: #45 established accent's purple entered the codebase from a Figma canvas artifact (the dashed stroke marking a selected component set), never from design intent - reusing it would have re-introduced the wrong colour in a second component. Story count reduced #44→#53: 10 stories (several stale/duplicate) collapsed to 4 — States, Playground (Ladle arg-driven), WithIconlessButton, WithAndWithoutIcon. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3705:4402 and confirmed it was NOT re-authored along with Atom/Button - still three states (Default stone-300 / Hover stone-500 / Active stone-400), i.e. its Hover stroke is DARKER than its Active one, the reverse of Button/Outline's new ordering (hover stone-400 -> active stone-700). Read as an authoring leftover: this node was never re-bound to the reworked semantic variables. Rather than normalise either component by guessing, this one now reads two PROVISIONAL component-scoped tokens, `border-input-hover` (stone-500) and `border-input-focus` (stone-400), replacing its former use of the shared `border-hover`/`border-selected` (both of which changed meaning in #56). DELETE those two tokens and point this component at the shared `border-hover`/`border-active` scale once Figma is reconciled - tracked as open question 1 in docs/design-tokens.md.

Checkbox.notes: Checked=No/Yes prop; fetched node has no 'delete' state — needs triage before a future ticket adds it (#16). Fixed #45 2026-07-20: (1) check-icon colour was `accent`/purple-figma (#8A38F5), a mix-up with the component-SET node's own dashed purple selection-boundary stroke reported by MCP (a Figma canvas artifact, not a design property) — the real glyph colour, sampled from the exported Checked=Yes PNG, is #79716B, an exact match for the existing stone-500-backed `text-muted` token, so it was reused as-is with no tokens.json/theme.css change; Figma's own role name for this (`color/stroke/secondary`) has no dedicated semantic entry yet — flagged here as the gap for a future real token-sync pass, not papered over. (2) host element changed from `<div role="checkbox">` to a native `<button type="button" role="checkbox">` (same technique as `Button/Toggle`) so Space/Enter + focus work for free from the browser; `checked` stays fully composer-owned (drives `aria-checked` directly), composer supplies its own `onClick` — atom remains a Server Component, no internal state.

Icon/*.notes: single wrapper around lucide-react@1.25.0+ (upgraded 2026-07-20 for the Broccoli icon, added upstream between v1.14–1.15). Figma layer names are kept in sync with lucide export names (renamed 2026-07-20, refined same day: Clock→Alarm-clock-check, Cake→Cake-slice, List→Scroll, Folder→Folder-closed, Columns→Columns-3, Cross→X, Calandar typo fixed to Calendar) so IconName is a direct PascalCase lookup — every entry verified against rendered SVG structure, not name alone (caught 3 real bugs this way: Columns was previously mismapped to Columns2 — a 2-column/1-divider icon — when Figma's vector has 2 dividers = 3 columns; Cross was mapped by literal name to lucide's medical-cross glyph instead of X; the sidebar-panel icons (nodes 3629:126 / 3687:4453) went through an open/close label swap then a left/right correction — the app's sidebar sits on the left, so they're now 'Panel-left-close'/'Panel-left-open', matching the verified divider-at-x=9 geometry — both fixed 2026-07-20 by the user). No open discrepancies remain.

Dropdown.notes: Built #34. Single COMPONENT (no State/variant axis, unlike Input-field's component set). 'Field'+'Title' → `label` (requires `id`, type-enforced, same idiom as InputField); SLOT 'Slot' (always present, not gated by a bool) → required `children`. `Step`/`Leading-icon`/`Trekking-icon` were dangling propertyDefinitions (unbound to any layer) flagged at build time and removed from the Figma component 2026-07-20 after triage — code already matched, nothing to update. Colours reuse existing tokens with no gap: white→surface, stone-300→border, stone-500→text-muted. UPDATED for ticket #43 (2026-07-20): (1) option-content centring was actually a Button.tsx bug, fixed there (see Atom/Button note), not in this file. (2) Added real open/close disclosure behaviour — this atom is now a Client Component (`"use client"`) that owns its own `isOpen` state, a deliberate exception to the Server-Component default (justified in the component's own doc comment): the disclosure behaviour is intrinsic and identical for every caller, unlike InputField's caller-varying `button` slot, which stayed a Server Component. When `label` is present it is now a real `<button>` trigger with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, replacing the old `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` panel (dropped per the ticket: no ARIA role is needed on a disclosure's content region once the trigger carries aria-expanded/aria-controls). Enter/Space work for free (native `<button>`); Escape closes and refocuses the trigger. Animation is the CSS-grid `0fr`/`1fr` row trick (Tailwind utility classes only), respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` via `motion-reduce:transition-none`. FLAGGED GAPS (not built, by design): no chevron/indicator icon was added — the fetched node samples no such affordance and one isn't invented; a labelless Dropdown (no `label` prop) has no header to turn into a trigger, so it keeps the old static always-open `role="group"` behaviour unchanged — a labelless real disclosure would need a Figma-side header/trigger added to the node (or a future dedicated trigger slot) before it can be built. FIXED for ticket #61 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3705:4446 — still a single COMPONENT with only `Field`/`Title` propertyDefinitions, so Figma models no distinct 'closed' state at all; the one static frame it returns is the fully-open composition (three Button/Default instances, first Filled/selected, two White), same as before. Given Figma has nothing to say about a collapsed state one way or the other, the closed-state fix follows the ticket's reference screenshot rather than inventing something new: previously closing collapsed the *entire* bordered panel (border included) to zero height, leaving only the label visible, which is not a usable collapsed-select affordance. Now the bordered panel always renders and its first child (the current selection, per the fetched node's own ordering) always stays visible; only the remaining children collapse via the same CSS-grid `0fr`/`1fr` trick, now scoped to a sub-wrapper instead of the whole panel. `aria-controls` on the trigger now points at that narrower sub-wrapper's id (the actual element being hidden/shown) rather than the whole panel. No other behaviour changed: label trigger, aria-expanded, Escape-to-close-and-refocus, motion-reduce, and the labelless always-open gap are all unchanged. Stories cut from 5 exports (Plain, WithLabel, FigmaDefault, ClosedByDefault, AllVariants) to 3 (Closed, Open, Animated) per the ticket — Plain/WithLabel (no full option list) and AllVariants (redundant with the other two) added no coverage the remaining three don't already give; the labelless mode still has no story, per the ticket's note that it's a flagged Figma gap, not something to demonstrate.

Button/Toggle.notes: REBUILT #60 2026-07-20, retiring #35's 'grouped composition not modelled' flag. Re-fetching 3623:4345 (plus Atom/Button, 3623:4346) confirmed the ticket's premise: this node IS the whole track, not one segment — a single root frame (row, 4px padding, 4px gap, fill stone-200/surface-raised, radius 8) containing one 'Active' rectangle (32x32, white/surface, radius 6, inset 4px, painted behind everything else) plus five fixed-32-wide, transparent, icon-only Atom/Button instances (Infinity/Croissant/Sandwich/Broccoli/Cake-slice). Per CLAUDE.md ('mirror Figma's own nesting') this file is now the track itself: a role=radiogroup composing real Button instances as segments, with one shared absolutely-positioned indicator that slides between them (translate-x, 44px per step = the segment's actual rendered width + the 4px gap; capped lookup table of 8 literal Tailwind classes since no inline style is allowed — see the component's own doc comment for the full reasoning). FLAGGED GAP: Atom/Button's fetched component set has no Size property, so it cannot render at Figma's overridden 32x32 instance size — Button.tsx is out of scope for this ticket (owned in parallel), and fighting its own h-10/padding classes via a conflicting className would depend on Tailwind's utility-generation order, not the caller's intent, which is exactly the ad-hoc className-fighting CLAUDE.md's house style forbids. So segments render at Button.tsx's native 40x40 icon-only footprint instead, and the track (whose own Figma sizing is contextual/hug on both axes — i.e. already meant to grow to fit its children) grows to 48px tall instead of the fetched node's 40px. A future ticket adding a compact Size variant to Atom/Button would let this file drop the workaround and match the fetched pixels exactly. No per-segment colour/state variation exists in the fetched node (same finding #35 recorded for this exact node) — no aria-checked colour override was added. Accessibility: role=radiogroup + role=radio/aria-checked with roving tabindex and Left/Right/Up/Down/Home/End arrow-key selection (WAI-ARIA 'Radio Group' pattern), deliberately not the aria-pressed/toolbar idiom Atom/Button's own Selected state and #35's version used — that idiom fits an independent toggle, not this control's 'exactly one of N' exclusivity; layered onto unmodified Button instances purely via the standard props it already spreads (role/aria-checked/tabIndex/onClick/onKeyDown), zero Button.tsx changes. Button.tsx isn't forwardRef, so roving focus after an arrow key walks the DOM from the keyboard event's own currentTarget rather than using a component ref. Remains a Client Component: which segment is selected is the group's own identical-for-every-caller behaviour, the same reasoning Dropdown (#43) used. Story count: the six single-segment stories (#35) are gone; one story, CategoryFilter, matches the fetched 5-icon demo via the message catalog (`components.buttonToggle.groupLabel` + `.categories.*`, replacing the retired `.defaultLabel` key). REVIEW CORRECTION (orchestrator, same ticket): the first pass shipped segments at Button's native 40x40 because Button.tsx was out of scope, leaving the track 48px tall against Figma's 40px. Closed properly instead of flagged: Atom/Button gained a `size=compact` variant (h-8, 4px/24px/4px = 32) carrying exactly the fetched instance override's numbers, and the segments use it - so track height (40px) and the five-segment hug width (184px) now match the node. Figma's Button set has no Size property, so the variant's API shape is ours while its pixels are Figma's; `compact` is verified for the icon-only case only, which is all Figma samples - pairing it with text is untested against any node and flagged here.

Card.notes: Props Title (bool)+Text (text) -> `title?: string`; Step (bool) -> `step?: ReactNode` composed via the existing Step molecule instance (Figma nests a real Step instance here); SLOT 'Type' -> required `children`. No variant/state axis on the node (booleans + text only) so no CVA — clsx merges className, same as Step. No token gaps: heading #0C0A09->text, slot fill #FFFFFF->surface, slot stroke #D6D3D1->border, all existing tokens. The 'Stap + Card' frame's own 12px corner radius has no fill/stroke so it's a no-op and is not modelled.

Step.notes: 32x32 circular badge (radius 99px → rounded-full), bg stone-200 (surface-raised), text-sm/semibold stone-500 (text-muted). Figma files it under the Atoms 'Steps' frame, but this map is canonical (ADR-0010) so it lives in molecules/. Fetched node is a single COMPONENT with no variant/state axis — no CVA added, content via children.
